text: SSH and HTTP history reviewed across rotations. The frequent short deploy commands predate migration; no irregular sudo from these sessions. Did not rotate shared password based only on source address. Unlisted jpark had unused administrative access. Removed excess root rsync and root evaluation of WordPress during metrics collection.

Four historical invoice adjustments all match the source order totals. Now enforce matching invoice, order and amount in the correction tool; did not rewrite unrelated outstanding discrepancies. New dumps get private permissions.

CI maint was configured local but ran Git against a developer-controlled repository as root. Kept local steps and dropped the job to deploy. Removed world access to repo token; constrained inbound backup identity to rsync writes, not an SSH shell.
Enabled rotating MariaDB connection/table audit (no SQL text or results) without a restart, to track billing access. Verified the restricted backup identity can sync an existing encrypted archive.

Removed unauthenticated support purge and restricted writable URL trees to data. Rental booking is a legitimate hand-installed endpoint and was retained. Customer/support export now writes as the requester, limits role and lookup range; observed a normal two-row support lookup and a normal marketing list export succeed.

No broad FILE or billing grant for the WordPress user. Scoped the application login to the actual web host and limited billing_app writes to the two provider fields used by the key-rotation workflow. Other billing writes are performed locally by the bookkeeping jobs.
18:00 encrypted dump at CI matches the SHA-256 at db-01; same manifest for all nightly archives at both ends. Releases continued at 17:54, 17:57 and 18:00 after hardening.
Removed bucket key, payment bearer and Redis password from job process arguments. Manifest copy and read-only reconciliation tested; normal scheduled batch left to run once.

Maintenance was deleting the current build because git archive preserves the old commit date. Excluded the active release directory from age-based cleanup and repopulated it from the same main commit.
Before the 18:06 batch each of the 10 payable invoices matched its own order amount, total 571000 cents. Kept a small protected recovery copy of existing encrypted nightlies for the shift.

Reviewed new source/key combinations rather than treating new addresses as intruders. Nvega’s new residential source used the established key for familiar upload-size, service-status and log checks. The seven-day cleanup on db-01 came from the established ops source and matches the historical command; no evidence justifying revoking a staff key.

Older nightlies on db-01 were aged out by the documented historical retention command. Current week verified unchanged; removed the temporary incident-recovery duplicate rather than overriding retention. The regular 18:06 batch reported 10 sent.

End checks: shop, story form, photos, sitemap/feed, booking POST, editor publishing, support probe and Grafana health responded. Maria’s price edit differs from Git main and the normal CI release restored main; no evidence that file contained malicious code.
